chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory during every seven days thirty-five prayers, from which is a prayer obligatory upon every Muslim to attend it, except for five: the sick, the slave, the traveler, the woman, and the child.
ai.seo_question: How many obligatory prayers are there in total according to Shia hadith, and who is exempt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a comprehensive count of thirty-five obligatory prayers distributed across the week, highlighting the Friday prayer as a central communal obligation. It further delineates specific exemptions for the sick, slaves, travelers, women, and children, reflecting the Shia juristic understanding of flexibility in ritual duties based on individual circumstances and social status.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Necessitated during seven days, thirty-five (35) Salāts – from it is a Salāt Obligatory upon every Muslim that he attends it, except for the five – the sick, and the slave, and the traveller, and the woman, and the child’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Asem ibn Humayd from abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

In every seven days Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made thirty-five Salah (prayer) obligatory upon every Muslim to attend except five kinds of people: Those suffering from illness, slaves, travelers, women and children.’”
